name: security-content-type-parser-selection-review
intent: Content-Type and body-decoder disagreement at security checks
artifacts: Route decoder selection, accepted media types, validation middleware, raw bytes and final business consumer.
trace: Follow whether authentication, CSRF or schema checks inspect the same representation later consumed by the handler. Include content-type parameters and fallback decoders only when reachable.
experiment: Use two harmless representations of one owned operation and compare the authorized baseline with one policy-relevant decoder variation.
disproof: Merely accepting JSON and form data is not a flaw; a decoder error or unchanged denial does not show a security boundary crossed.
repair: Make accepted formats explicit and apply the security check to the consumed representation; retest intended formats and ambiguous rejection.
branch_decisions: Check accepted charset/structured-suffix and fallback decoding using the installed framework. A simple content type accepted as JSON can matter to CSRF only if the real authentication and state-change path allows it. Separate decoder disagreement, authorization failure and same-origin response-read claims.
